name: Igede
catalog_citation: Bergman, Richard. 1971. Vowel sandhi and word division in Igede. Journal of West African Languages 8(1):13-25.
catalog_locator: pp.15-16 (sec. 1.1 Phonology: Tones; Syllables and words); scanned PDF, no text layer, pages read visually
catalog_quote: Igede has a discrete level tone system with four level tones: high /´/, high-mid /¯/, low-mid (unmarked), and low /`/. Each vowel and syllabic nasal occurs with one of these four tones. Over 250 minimal pairs, triplets, quadruplets, and quintuplets have been found, involving 30 per cent of the total vocabulary collected (about 2,000 items). ... Phonemes combine to form syllables and phonological words. The syllable consists of V (vowel), CV (consonant, vowel), or N (syllabic nasal), each of which always occurs with a single tone. The word is equated with the vowel harmony unit.

sources.citation: Adeniyi, Kolawole. 2026. Synchronic variation in Igede syllable structure. Afrika und Übersee 99:1-24. DOI 10.15460/auue.2026.99.1.406 (CC-BY 4.0).
sources.quote: p.4: 'Typologically, vowel reduction has been shown to occur more in unstressed syllables (Sen 2012: 466). However, Igede lacks stress, which eliminates the place of stress in the case reported in this study.' p.6: 'There are four contrastive tones in Igede, the High <á>, high-mid <ā>, low-mid <ä>, and low <à> tones (Hartell 1993: 230).' and 'Igede has the CV, V, and N syllable types (Bergman 1971)... In a tone language, the syllabic nasal typically bears its own tone'.
sources.note: fetched sources now; supplies the explicit denial of stress ('Igede lacks stress', p.4) that the 1971 source lacks and should be added to the record as a corroborating text-layer source.

sources.citation: Abiodun, Michael. 1991. Vowel harmony in Igede. Studies in African Linguistics 22(2):157-169. DOI 10.32473/sal.v22i2.107422.
sources.quote: No statement about Igede stress or accent; the article treats the nine-vowel ATR harmony system. Tone marks are used on data throughout.
sources.locator: pp.157-169 (whole article; p.164 only generic mention of 'stress' as an autosegmental tier)

sources.quote: 'Tones: high, high-mid, low-mid, low. Tone is not written in the orthography except in a few minimal pairs.' Nothing on stress.
